source.title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages

accepted.question_text: For every space bound S(n) with S(n) at least log n, does nondeterministic space-bounded computation collapse to deterministic space-bounded computation; equivalently, is DSPACE(S(n)) = NSPACE(S(n)) for all S(n) >= log n? The paper also singles out the special case S(n) = n, asking whether deterministic and nondeterministic linear bounded automata have the same power.

evidence.quote: We define similarly the notions of operations within space S(n) and the classes NSPACE(S(n)) and DSPACE(S(n)). We also define P- TIME = U ~= 1D TIME(nk), NP" TIME = U~= ~ N TIME(nk), P-SPACE = U~= 1 DSPACE(nk), DLBA = DSPACE(n), NLBA = NSPACE(n), DLOG = DSPACE(logn) and N LOG = NSPACE(logn).
1. Is DSPACE(S(n)) = NSPACE(S(n)) for all S(n) >_ logn ?2 The special case S(n) = n is called "the LBA problem" and has been studied for over ten years

accepted.question_text: Does deterministic polynomial time equal nondeterministic polynomial time, that is, is every language in NP-TIME also in P-TIME so that P-TIME = NP-TIME?

evidence.quote: We also define P- TIME = U ~= 1D TIME(nk), NP" TIME = U~= ~ N TIME(nk)
2. Is P-TIME = NP-TIME?

accepted.question_text: Does deterministic polynomial time coincide with deterministic polynomial space, i.e., is P-TIME = P-SPACE?

evidence.quote: We also define P- TIME = U ~= 1D TIME(nk), NP" TIME = U~= ~ N TIME(nk), P-SPACE = U~= 1 DSPACE(nk)
3. Is P-TIME = P-SPACE?

accepted.question_text: Does deterministic polynomial time collapse all the way to deterministic logarithmic space, meaning P-TIME = DLOG where DLOG denotes DSPACE(log n)?

evidence.quote: We also define P- TIME = U ~= 1D TIME(nk), NP" TIME = U~= ~ N TIME(nk), P-SPACE = U~= 1 DSPACE(nk), DLBA = DSPACE(n), NLBA = NSPACE(n), DLOG = DSPACE(logn) and N LOG = NSPACE(logn).
4. Is P-TIME = DLOG?

accepted.question_text: Is deterministic polynomial time contained in some polylogarithmic-space deterministic class; equivalently, does there exist an exponent i such that every language in P-TIME lies in DSPACE((log n)^i)?

evidence.quote: 5. Is P-TIME ~ DSPACE ((logn) i) for some i?

accepted.question_text: If a Turing machine is allowed an auxiliary pushdown stack whose space is not counted toward the work-tape bound, does that extra stack add computational power over ordinary deterministic space-bounded computation? In the notation of the paper, is PDM(S(n)) = DSPACE(S(n)) for all S(n) >= log n?

evidence.quote: In [4] Cook has introduced the notion of pdm(S(n)), i.e. a TM using a pushdown stack and operating within space S(n) (not counting the space used by the stack).
6. Is PDM(S(n)) = DSPACE(S(n)) for all S(n) > logn?

accepted.question_text: Does the class 2DPDA of languages accepted by one-head two-way deterministic pushdown automata coincide with the class DLBA = DSPACE(n) of languages accepted by deterministic linear bounded automata?

evidence.quote: DLBA = DSPACE(n)
Let 2DPDA(k) = {L|L = L(A) for some 2dpda(k) A}. We will be interested primarily in the case k = 1, in which case the automaton is called a 2dpda and the class of language is 2DPDA.
1. Is 2DPDA = DLBA?

accepted.question_text: Does 2DPDA coincide with 2DC, where 2DC is the class of languages accepted by one-head two-way deterministic counter machines?

evidence.quote: The abbreviation 2dc (2nc) denotes a 2dpda (2ndpa) which is allowed only one stack symbol plus a bottom of a stack marker. lnc will stand for a one-way nondeterministic counter machine. The class 2DC (2NC, 1NC) is defined in the obvious way.
the automaton is called a 2dpda and the class of language is 2DPDA.
2. Is 2DPDA = 2DC?

accepted.question_text: Do one-head two-way deterministic counter machines and one-head two-way nondeterministic counter machines accept exactly the same languages; in other words, is 2DC = 2NC?

evidence.quote: The abbreviation 2dc (2nc) denotes a 2dpda (2ndpa) which is allowed only one stack symbol plus a bottom of a stack marker. lnc will stand for a one-way nondeterministic counter machine. The class 2DC (2NC, 1NC) is defined in the obvious way.
3. Is 2DC = 2NC?

accepted.question_text: What is the exact relationship between the class 2NC of languages accepted by one-head two-way nondeterministic counter machines and the deterministic log-space class DLOG = DSPACE(log n)?

evidence.quote: DLOG = DSPACE(logn)
The abbreviation 2dc (2nc) denotes a 2dpda (2ndpa) which is allowed only one stack symbol plus a bottom of a stack marker.
4. What is the relationship between 2NC and DLOG?

accepted.question_text: What is the exact relationship between the class 2DPDA of languages accepted by one-head two-way deterministic pushdown automata and the deterministic log-space class DLOG = DSPACE(log n)?

evidence.quote: DLOG = DSPACE(logn)
the automaton is called a 2dpda and the class of language is 2DPDA.
5. What is the relationship between 2DPDA and DLOG?

accepted.question_text: Do one-head two-way nondeterministic pushdown automata and one-head two-way deterministic pushdown automata accept the same languages; equivalently, is 2NPDA = 2DPDA?

evidence.quote: A two-way nondeterministic k-head pushdown automaton, 2npda(k) ... A 2dpda(k) is defined as above, except that at most one choice of move is defined for each (k + 2)-tuple of state input symbols, and stack symbol.
A very important question--namely "is 2NPDA = 2DPDA ?"--is missing. We could not relate it to any of the open problems.

accepted.question_text: Is there a general method to decide, for a language already known to be accepted either by a one-head two-way deterministic pushdown automaton or by a one-way nondeterministic counter machine, whether that language also belongs to deterministic log-space DLOG?

evidence.quote: DLOG = DSPACE(logn)
lnc will stand for a one-way nondeterministic counter machine.
(1) Does a given 2dpda-language (lnc-language), L, belong to DLOG?

accepted.question_text: Given a specified family of languages, can one decide whether at least one member of that family belongs to 2DPDA, the class of languages accepted by one-head two-way deterministic pushdown automata?

evidence.quote: the automaton is called a 2dpda and the class of language is 2DPDA.
(2) Does one of a given family of languages belong to 2DPDA ?

accepted.question_text: Given a specified family of languages each already known to be a 2dpda-language or a 2nc-language, can one decide whether at least one member of that family belongs to 2DC, the class of languages accepted by one-head two-way deterministic counter machines?

evidence.quote: The class 2DC (2NC, 1NC) is defined in the obvious way.
(3) Does one of a family of 2dpda-languages (2nc-languages) belong to 2DC?
